content.title: About
content.content: Classic mixed vegetables, cooked, is a ready‑to‑serve side dish consisting of carrots, broccoli, cauliflower, green peas and corn that have been steamed or blanched. The vegetables retain their natural flavor, bright color, and most of their nutrients.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The mix usually includes 5–7 different vegetables, providing a wide range of vitamins and minerals.
Steaming preserves up to 90 % of vitamin C and most antioxidants.
The blend is popular in diet plans because it is low in calories (about 35 kcal per 100 g).
Combining different vegetables improves the absorption of certain nutrients, such as carrot beta‑carotene together with fats from olive oil.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Provides vitamin B6, folate and niacin, which support metabolism and the nervous system.

items.title: Source of dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion, promotes satiety and supports a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Broccoli and cauliflower contain glucosinolates, while carrots provide beta‑carotene, helping protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Low in fat and calories
items.content: Makes an ideal choice for weight management and cardiovascular health.

items.title: Immune support
items.content: Vitamin C from broccoli and peas boosts the body’s immune response.

items.title: Allergy to individual vegetables
items.content: Some individuals may react to broccoli, cauliflower or peas.

items.title: Nutrient loss with overcooking
items.content: Prolonged cooking can reduce vitamin content, especially vitamin C.

items.title: Sodium content in restaurant‑prepared dishes
items.content: If the vegetables are seasoned with salt, consider total sodium intake.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the vegetables as a side dish, add them to salads, soups, stews, or use them as a base for vegetarian meals. They reheat well in the microwave or sautéed briefly with a little olive oil.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. When frozen, they retain quality for 2‑3 months; thaw in the fridge before use.
